Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business and general-news outlets are dominated by a sharp AI-driven tech stock selloff and the record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack, with secondary focus on OpenAI and Anthropic's shifting fundraising fortunes, the ECB's leadership transition, and jittery markets ahead of the US midterms.

stories.headline: Tech Selloff Deepens as AI Trade Cracks Widen
stories.summary: A three-week rout in technology shares intensified, with WSJ noting Intel suffered its worst-ever daily decline as investor anxiety over AI spending hit new highs; Bloomberg reported the Nasdaq 100 tumbled 3.5% Friday, its deepest slide since June, as disappointing earnings from Amazon and Intel fed a broader rotation out of the AI trade.

stories.headline: Binance Hit by Record $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist Linked to North Korea
stories.summary: Hackers drained roughly $6.3 billion from Binance in about 20 minutes in what security researchers call the biggest crypto theft in history, with TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributing the attack with high confidence to the North Korean hacking unit TraderTraitor; Binance says it will cover all losses and has frozen about $3 billion of the stolen funds.

stories.headline: OpenAI Slashes Fundraising Target by $10 Billion
stories.summary: OpenAI is now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from a prior $30 billion target, as Bloomberg reported the pullback reflects mounting tech anxieties and the pressure of rival Anthropic's impending public listing.

stories.headline: Anthropic May Miss Investment-Grade Rating After IPO, Blackstone Warns
stories.summary: Blackstone says the AI lab is now expected to receive only a "high" junk rating rather than investment-grade status, a shift from earlier guidance that adds to scrutiny of Anthropic's finances as it pursues a public offering that could value it near $2 trillion.

stories.headline: Christine Lagarde's ECB Exit Sets Off High-Stakes Succession Race
stories.summary: NYT reports the looming departure of ECB president Christine Lagarde has triggered a search for a successor requiring both economic expertise and political acumen, while WSJ frames her next chapter as a defense of waning globalist politics and the Economist warns her successor inherits the job at "a moment of peril."

stories.headline: US Midterms Loom Over Jittery Investors
stories.summary: FT says caution is warranted for markets in the coming weeks as the midterm elections add another layer of uncertainty on top of the AI-driven selloff, while Politico reports Republicans are bracing for "once-unthinkable losses" and record political ad spending.

stories.headline: China's Economic Activity Loses Steam Sharply in October
stories.summary: WSJ reports a sharp slowdown in Chinese economic activity for October, adding to global growth concerns as markets already contend with the tech selloff.

stories.headline: Getty Images Restructuring Hits SPAC Warrant Snag
stories.summary: Puck reports the Getty and Koch families moved aggressively to take Getty Images private and avoid prolonged bankruptcy, but warrants issued when the company went public via SPAC in 2022 have created legal complications now occupying a dozen advisory firms.

Business.gaps: No recent distinct coverage found from Forbes or The Information beyond AI-funding context already folded into other stories; Business Insider had no relevant feed items or search results.

US politics.overview: Coverage across political outlets is dominated by the final stretch before Tuesday's midterms, with handicappers increasingly bullish on a Democratic House takeover, Republicans privately bracing for steep losses, and the Trump DOJ waging an unusually aggressive pre-election legal campaign over noncitizen voting and the Alaska Senate race. Affordability, healthcare costs, and the Alaska 'spoiler candidate' controversy are also recurring threads, alongside Supreme Court cases and Democrats' mixed reaction to Israel's elections.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report: Democrats favored to flip the House, could post historic gains
stories.summary: Cook's latest analysis argues 2026 is a 'reversion' election in which previously Trump-trending, blue-collar and Hispanic-heavy districts are swinging back to Democrats, putting the party on the brink of an anti-Trump wave even bigger than 2018's. The nonpartisan handicapper now projects Democrats could flip between roughly a dozen and two dozen House seats.

stories.headline: Trump's DOJ escalates pre-election legal offensive, including bid to delay Alaska certification
stories.summary: Axios details a wave of politically charged DOJ actions just before the midterms, including a lawsuit seeking to delay certifying Alaska's Senate race if Republican Dan Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, plus investigations touching Ilhan Omar, Lisa Cook and a Virginia state senator. A federal judge separately ordered the administration to stop threatening election officials with prosecution over noncitizen-voting claims.

stories.headline: House Republicans privately brace for a possible 'blowout' on Election Day
stories.summary: Despite Speaker Mike Johnson's public confidence, Punchbowl reports panic inside the House GOP conference as polling shows margin-of-error races even in deep-red districts Trump won by double digits, forcing outside groups to retreat from some incumbents entirely.

stories.headline: Alaska's 'two Dan Sullivans' spoiler controversy roils the Senate majority fight
stories.summary: Alaska's governor has ordered an investigation into allegations that Democrats recruited a second, similarly named candidate to siphon votes from GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan, a scheme Republicans call a bombshell and the DOJ has cited in seeking to delay certification if the incumbent loses.

stories.headline: Trump reverses course, revives in-person rallies for final midterm push
stories.summary: Trump scrapped plans to replace rallies with tele-townhalls but reversed within a day and flew to South Carolina and is now headed to Iowa and Kansas, as his political team scrambles to shore up vulnerable incumbents like Lindsey Graham and Roger Marshall in the campaign's closing days.

stories.headline: Affordability and healthcare costs loom over midterm voting
stories.summary: NPR examines how affordability questions—from a Florida ballot measure on homeowner versus public-service funding to double-digit premium hikes on Healthcare.gov—are shaping voter decisions nationwide just before Election Day.

stories.headline: Supreme Court opens new argument session with high-stakes cases, including a test for Omar's expulsion push
stories.summary: The justices begin a November sitting featuring several criminal-law arguments and a habeas case on when a legal rule counts as 'previously unavailable,' while separately Fox News reports Trump's push to oust Rep. Ilhan Omar is headed for a Supreme Court test that legal experts call legally uncertain.

stories.headline: Democrats on Capitol Hill weigh mixed signals from Israel's elections
stories.summary: House Democrats are expressing relief at high turnout in Israel's elections this week but remain uncertain about the broader implications, reflecting a party still grappling with internal divisions over Israel policy heading into the midterms.

US politics.gaps: NYT and WSJ had no relevant feed items and are blocked from direct search, so no current coverage from them could be confirmed. The Guardian and Politico are also search-blocked; only their provided feed items (mostly general or tangential to US politics) were available.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage this cycle is dominated by cracks in the AI financing boom: a sharp tech stock selloff, OpenAI cutting its fundraising target, Anthropic's weak expected credit rating, and lenders pulling back from AI infrastructure debt. A parallel thread covers AI security incidents (a backdoored Claude extension on Cursor) and industry moves on data scraping, model safety, and workforce restructuring at Microsoft, alongside Google DeepMind's new Genie 4 world-model launch.

stories.headline: Wall Street's 'AI wake-up call' sends tech stocks tumbling
stories.summary: A bruising selloff in technology shares has fueled concern that the AI-driven stock rally may be overextended, compounded by Intel's worst-ever daily decline and disappointing Amazon results.

stories.headline: OpenAI slashes funding target from $30B to roughly $20B
stories.summary: OpenAI has cut back its fundraising ambitions, now seeking about $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation after securing only around $11 billion in commitments, as investor appetite for AI bets cools.

stories.headline: Anthropic expected to get only 'high junk' credit rating after IPO
stories.summary: Blackstone now expects Anthropic to receive a high junk rather than investment-grade rating from credit agencies post-IPO, a shift that could make it costlier for the AI lab to keep funding its massive spending.

stories.headline: Lenders shut neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale out of bond markets
stories.summary: Three major AI-infrastructure 'neoclouds' have effectively been frozen out of bond markets in recent weeks as lenders and investors demand tougher terms, signaling a new, costlier phase for the AI data-center build-out.

stories.headline: Backdoored Claude Code extension sat on Cursor's marketplace for hours
stories.summary: A tampered copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension was live on Cursor's marketplace for nearly 12 hours and attempted remote access and data theft, affecting up to roughly 5,000 users; Anthropic says it did not build or publish the compromised version.

stories.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back new AI-scraping opt-out standard
stories.summary: The four companies say they will adopt a shared technical standard that lets publishers more easily signal they don't want their content scraped for AI training.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary severance to a quarter of its workforce
stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees — roughly 25% of staff — in its second such program this year, while protecting teams seen as critical to its AI push.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a new real-time interactive world model
stories.summary: DeepMind announced Genie 4, a natively multimodal world model with native audio and improved physics simulation, rolling it out first as a research preview to trusted testers.

Tech & AI.gaps: Could not independently verify recent coverage from The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, The Economist, or The Guardian beyond what was in the provided feed items, since these outlets block web search.

Energy.overview: Coverage across energy and climate outlets is dominated by Middle East oil-supply jitters, a fast-moving fight over U.S. permitting reform (BAAJA) and transmission, and growing alarm about AI data centers' strain on the grid and emissions. Utility Dive and Latitude Media are heavy on utility earnings/capex and data-center power deals, while Carbon Brief looks ahead to COP31 and Heatmap and others track lawsuits over Trump administration offshore wind deals.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise as Hormuz tanker attack and Houthi claims stoke supply fears
stories.summary: Oil prices rose as markets weighed possible military escalation in the Middle East after a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi claims, compounded by the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.
also_covered_by: WSJ (separate piece on U.S. military's Gulf shipping protection mission)

stories.headline: AI data centers' gas plants set to emit as much CO2 as all of Mexico by 2030
stories.summary: A new Sierra Club analysis reported by Heatmap finds fossil-fueled power plants built to run AI data centers are on track to emit 460 million metric tons of CO2 by 2030, erasing roughly 15 years of U.S. power-sector emissions reductions.

stories.headline: Senate's BAAJA permitting bill wins broad praise for transmission overhaul
stories.summary: Heatmap details how the bipartisan permitting bill's transmission section is drawing support from clean-energy groups, utilities and even past critics, with modeling suggesting it could meaningfully expand grid capacity and cut emissions.

stories.headline: What China wants from the COP31 climate talks
stories.summary: With the COP31 summit in Turkey approaching, Carbon Brief surveys experts on what priorities Beijing is expected to push at the talks.

stories.headline: New York and California sue over Trump administration's offshore wind cancellation deals
stories.summary: New York and California filed new lawsuits challenging Interior Department deals that paid developers to cancel offshore wind projects, with officials calling the payouts an abuse of taxpayer funds that will set back clean energy.

stories.headline: Chinese-linked solar developer loses appeal over Texas grid interconnection
stories.summary: A federal appeals court ruled Texas has a free hand to enforce restrictions on foreign-owned companies' access to its electric grid, upholding the state's block on a Chinese-linked solar project's interconnection.

stories.headline: Utilities supercharge capital spending plans as data-center demand surges
stories.summary: Xcel Energy rolled out a $70 billion, five-year capital plan heavy on renewables and storage, while American Electric Power separately raised its own investment plan by 30% after its contracted data-center load jumped 22%.

stories.headline: AI stock selloff ripples into clean energy and gas-power markets
stories.summary: WSJ reports that cracks in the AI trade triggered a sharp tech selloff, a theme Latitude Media also explored in looking at how the AI stock slide and slowing gas-turbine orders are hitting clean energy markets.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media had no recent items in the feed and could not be reached via search in this pass. E&E News search results returned only older archived stories, not clearly from the last 24-48 hours, so current E&E News coverage could not be confirmed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage this week is dominated by the conclusion of the Communist Party's Fifth Plenum, which enacted an anti-corruption/discipline resolution and confirmed a record purge of senior officials, alongside signs of a cooling Chinese economy (weak October factory data) and a wave of tech and auto-sector business news, from Apple's AI rollout with Alibaba to Geely's earnings miss. Hong Kong outlets continue to focus heavily on political fallout from the deadly Tai Po fire, while security-related US-China friction (spying allegations, Taiwan) also features prominently.

stories.headline: CPC Fifth Plenum concludes with party self-governance resolution, record 33 officials expelled
stories.summary: State-run Xinhua reports the Communist Party's Central Committee wrapped up its four-day fifth plenum by adopting a resolution on 'persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance' and confirming earlier Politburo decisions to punish violators, while Zhang Shengmin was elected to the Politburo. Hong Kong Free Press and Taipei Times note the session confirmed the expulsion of a record 33 officials, including former top general Zhang Youxia, leaving what one outlet called an unusually high number of empty Central Committee seats.

stories.headline: China's factory activity contracts for third time in four months
stories.summary: Nikkei Asia (via Reuters) reports China's official manufacturing PMI for October fell to 49.3 from 50.1 in September, an unexpected contraction driven by soft demand for exports and domestic goods. WSJ separately reported that broader Chinese economic activity 'lost steam sharply' in October, underscoring a faltering recovery despite earlier export strength.

stories.headline: Apple Intelligence to launch in China in December via Alibaba's Qwen
stories.summary: SCMP reports Apple's long-awaited AI features will officially launch on iPhones in China in December, ending two years of regulatory uncertainty as Apple partners with Alibaba. State-run Global Times adds that the Qwen integration lets Chinese users access AI tools via Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, with features available for developer testing from November 4 and public release with iOS 27.3 in December.

stories.headline: Geely's Q3 profit misses estimates as China's auto market slows
stories.summary: Caixin reports Geely's net profit rose 28% to 4.8 billion yuan in the third quarter but missed analyst expectations of 5.5–6 billion yuan, as mounting competition and weakening domestic demand weighed on results, sending shares down 4.37%. The company's overseas sales surged 169% to 798,000 vehicles in nine months, but new EU hybrid-vehicle export quotas are prompting Geely to pursue localized manufacturing with Volvo.

stories.headline: Hong Kong officials resist resignation calls over Tai Po fire inquiry findings
stories.summary: Hong Kong Free Press reports the city's security chief defended remaining in his post after the Wang Fuk Court fire inquiry, saying his duty to the city outweighs personal interests, while the development chief separately likened herself to a sailor following a captain's orders when pressed on resignation calls. Authorities also announced about 300 civil servants from the disgraced inspection unit will be transferred to a new regulatory body, and the inquiry found insufficient evidence linking a district councillor to bid-rigging.

stories.headline: Beijing denies spying on Nvidia's Jensen Huang as US jails two Chinese nationals for military espionage attempt
stories.summary: Hong Kong Free Press reports Beijing dismissed as 'groundless speculation' a report claiming Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Separately, HKFP reports two Chinese nationals, Liren Lai and Yuance Chen, were sentenced to prison in California after admitting they tried to recruit US military service members to spy for Beijing.

stories.headline: Xiaomi invests $253 million in EV battery maker Sunwoda, deepening supply-chain ties
stories.summary: CnEVPost reports Xiaomi plans to invest about $253 million for a 5.34% stake in Sunwoda EVB, becoming its third-largest shareholder, following a similar move by Li Auto. TechNode confirms the deal involves a 1.7 billion yuan investment through Xiaomi's investment subsidiary, part of a broader push by Chinese EV makers to lock in battery supply.

stories.headline: Chinese ships mapping seabed data that could aid military operations near Taiwan
stories.summary: WSJ reports a flurry of Chinese ships were recently sent to map the seabed in waters around Taiwan, in research that Taiwanese officials say amounts to 'battlespace preparation.'

China.gaps: Could not retrieve recent items from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, CGTN, Yicai Global or Focus Taiwan; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and The Economist block search so coverage is limited to feed items provided for those outlets, none of which were in this group's feed.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by the grinding US-Israel-Iran war, with renewed tanker attacks and claimed mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz dominating live blogs, alongside Israel's unresolved election deadlock and warnings from Egypt and Gulf officials about the risk of wider escalation. Business outlets are tracking how the conflict is reshaping Gulf oil strategy, labour policy and regional growth forecasts.

stories.headline: Iran claims multiple tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz as attacks intensify
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported that three oil tankers exploded after hitting sea mines while navigating an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz, with vessels said to have switched off radar and ignored warnings, while US Central Command rejected Iran's separate claim of destroying an American sea drone, saying all its unmanned vessels remained accounted for. The National separately reported that October saw the highest number of attacks on ships transiting Hormuz since the war began, underscoring how a UN official is warning the world to 'adapt to higher prices' amid the standoff.

stories.headline: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs deadlocked, no majority for either side
stories.summary: With all votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 Knesset seats against 48 for Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc and 19 for Arab parties, leaving neither side able to form a majority government on its own, while Eisenkot's camp cannot govern without support from Arab-led factions. Haaretz reports Eisenkot has accused Netanyahu of leading an influence campaign to undermine the election results, as the stalemate drags on into a second week.

stories.headline: Egypt's foreign minister says new Iran war escalation would be 'more destructive' for the region
stories.summary: Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said he was extremely worried that a fresh escalation in the US-Iran war would hit the wider Middle East even harder, a warning he coupled with remarks that Gulf security cannot be separated from regional stability.

stories.headline: US military's nightly Hormuz missions straining aircraft and crews, report says
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal-sourced report cited by the Jerusalem Post says the US military's near-nightly operations to enforce the Hormuz blockade have succeeded but are putting growing strain on aircraft and crews.

stories.headline: Qatar's economy to jump 15 per cent in 2027 on gas sector recovery, S&P says
stories.summary: S&P projects Qatar's economy will grow sharply in 2027 as its gas sector rebounds, according to The National's report.

stories.headline: Gulf oil producers urged to guarantee crude supply as war reshapes energy markets
stories.summary: Industry experts say Gulf oil producers will retain their importance in global energy markets despite the Iran war, with one executive calling for stronger supply guarantees rather than discounts to keep customers confident. Separately, AGBI reported that Saudi Arabia is raising the minimum salary threshold for workers covered by a government employment-support programme to encourage more nationals into private-sector jobs.

stories.headline: UAE calls on world leaders to commit to water security at landmark Abu Dhabi summit
stories.summary: The UAE is pushing global leaders to make firm commitments on water security at a major summit being held in Abu Dhabi, according to The National.

stories.headline: Besieged by the Houthis, Yemen's Taiz teeters on the edge of humanitarian catastrophe
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post report describes how Houthi forces have cut off main routes into Taiz, leaving food stocks nearly depleted and hospitals close to running out of fuel.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not confirm distinct, within-48-hour coverage from Saudi Gazette, Zawya, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews or Iran International (search results for Iran International returned mostly older material). Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist and BBC coverage is reflected only through the provided feed items, since these outlets block web search.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Africa-focused outlets are converging on the deepening Ethiopia conflict and refugee crisis, South Africa's pivotal local elections, and fallout from the DRC-Rwanda war including new US sanctions. Business and tech coverage centers on African banks' capital strength, fintech innovation showcased at TechCabal's Moonshot event, and Angola's fiscal reforms.

stories.headline: Ethiopia conflict intensifies with drone strikes and mass civilian flight
stories.summary: Multiple drone strikes hit northern Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians including children, while Al Jazeera separately reports tens of thousands fleeing the fighting into Kenya.

stories.headline: South Africa's local elections pit Zille, Zuma and the ANC in a fight for the big cities
stories.summary: The ANC is defending its hold on major metros while the DA pushes into new territory and Zuma's MK party upends politics in KwaZulu-Natal ahead of the vote.

stories.headline: New US sanctions deepen the Congo-Rwanda standoff
stories.summary: Washington is ratcheting up pressure on Rwanda over the war in eastern DRC even as Kinshasa gains favour and US interest grows in Congo's critical minerals.

stories.headline: Angola to cut fuel subsidies without raising pump prices
stories.summary: Sub-Saharan Africa's second-largest oil producer plans to reduce 2027 subsidy spending while relying on other cost-cutting measures rather than price hikes.

stories.headline: African fintechs and banks race to go digital-first
stories.summary: Executives from Access Holdings and OPay told TechCabal's Moonshot conference in Lagos that banks must embed services invisibly into daily transactions to compete with digital platforms.

stories.headline: Tanzania marks one year since deadly election violence with calls for justice
stories.summary: A year on, demands for accountability over hundreds of killings during last year's disputed election continue to echo across Tanzania.

stories.headline: Ghana in talks with Russia for its first nuclear power plant
stories.summary: Following the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, Putin and Ghana's President Mahama held bilateral talks that included discussion of a nuclear energy partnership.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no recent dated items available beyond older archived issues; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block search so only items already in the provided feed (none for this beat) could be used.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past day centers on the AI-publishing wars — a court filing in the NYT/OpenAI case detailing the revenue hit from AI search, plus a celebrity-backed legal challenge and a new UK regulatory probe into Meta's scraping terms — alongside local-TV industry upheaval (Scripps layoffs), fallout from CBS's handling of a contested Senate race interview, and continued scrutiny of Paramount Skydance's finances and Trump's running feud with media figures.

stories.headline: Inside the '60' El-Sayed Scramble
stories.summary: Status reports that a CBS News correspondent's post cheering a GOP activist pressing Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on the Muslim Brotherhood threw a planned '60 Minutes' sit-down into flux, with producers reportedly also wary of editorial interference from Bari Weiss before the interview finally aired.

stories.headline: AI content retrieval 'already eating away' at publisher businesses, court told
stories.summary: Trade body Digital Content Next told a court that unique visitors to major US publishers fell a quarter between 2023 and 2025 as AI search tools rose, filing the data in support of the New York Times' copyright case against OpenAI and Microsoft, warning the trend amounts to a 'doom loop' for the industry.

stories.headline: Cate Blanchett-Led Coalition Challenges OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Battle
stories.summary: A coalition fronted by Cate Blanchett filed an amicus brief backing the New York Times in its copyright fight against OpenAI and Microsoft, with the Oscar winner arguing creators deserve control over use of their image and voice.

stories.headline: Scripps is cutting anchors and adding reporters. Is this the future of local TV news?
stories.summary: E.W. Scripps CEO Adam Symson announced a second wave of layoffs eliminating 431 positions as the company pushes a companywide transformation toward 'anchorless' local news built around more reporters.

stories.headline: Alaska Senate race controversy continues, puts election tactics in the spotlight
stories.summary: Poynter examines the fallout from a New York Times investigation into the Alaska Senate race involving Mary Peltola's campaign, with a companion Poynter piece detailing how the Times uncovered why there are two candidates named Dan Sullivan running.

stories.headline: UK competition watchdog opens investigation into Meta scraping terms
stories.summary: Britain's CMA has opened an inquiry into whether Meta's proposed terms for scraping publisher content could unfairly harm news organizations.

stories.headline: The Market Isn't Buying Skydance's Balance-Sheet Math
stories.summary: WSJ reports that Paramount Skydance's goodwill on its books now exceeds the company's entire stock-market value, raising investor doubts about its balance sheet.

stories.headline: Bill Maher Has Some Choice Words for Trump After His 1,300-Word Rant
stories.summary: Bill Maher pushed back on air after President Trump posted a lengthy Truth Social rant attacking him, with Maher joking the president 'went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store.'

Media.gaps: Puck: no dated story from the last 24-48 hours could be verified via search (site returned only static author/newsletter pages without recent timestamps). FT: no accessible recent coverage found; it blocks search and had no feed items. The Guardian and NYT also block search, so only their provided feed items (unrelated to this media-industry beat) were available.
